summary: Clean up stdio descendants after launcher exit

delivery.outcome: Terminate the owned POSIX stdio process group and release its worker/pipes after timeout even when the launcher already exited.
nonGoals: Do not claim the earlier intermittent test cause is proven
No deadline/assertion weakening, dependencies, cell logic, protocol or release changes
Preserve peer027 path quoting and every foreign checkout/lease

architecture.decision: Keep the owned POSIX process group cleanup independent of launcher liveness; retain the existing non-POSIX fallback, bounded wait/join and cache retirement. Add one actual-process regression with an exited launcher and live pipe-holding descendant.
architecture.rollback: Reviewed revert of the cleanup condition and its regression; retain the independently merged path quoting.

validation.evidence: Actual public-API exited-launcher regression fails before the repair and verifies worker/streams/cache cleanup after it; no request replay.
All existing assertions, host lifecycle controls and the peer027 path regressions remain valid.
Pinned networkless runtime verifies HTTP/gRPC/stdio, persistence and MCP with the original generated function unchanged.
Author delivery, exact-head required checks, independent review and protected merge; no manual merge or release.
